summary: All 14 occurrences checked. bləʕ swallowing differs from lqṭ snapping/seizing in PrS 24/27; do not infer swallowing from grasping alone.
Fronted feminine I ḥḏo is resumed by object -o in bləʕole; -le indexes the agent. The simple Preterit remains Preterit despite the edition’s anterior translation.

ko-bləʕla at 108/15 has a retained swallowing result with obstructing horns; the morphology supports ko-Preterit rather than Infectum boləʕ. The existing patient-oriented Detransitive Infectum at 3/36 is not duplicated.
PrS 24/23 repeats the inherited shark example cited prs 56/36. 29/332 and 115/210 also already occur in the entry.
No round-2 example or new sense is warranted. Jan 2.31/5166 repeats literal swallowing twice in one episode; R1 already filled the Preterit cell.

Jan 4.I/512 may use swallowing figuratively of a prior claim, but the clause is fragmented, bləʕʕe lacks transparent person segmentation, and lo mḥamalle does not resolve the intended acceptance/toleration. The machine English I swallowed it does not establish either.

PrS 75/128 lacks the swallowing translation within verse_translation. The reader joins the next verse in context_translation; that extra source text is not in the assigned verse. Supply the aligned continuation before adding an example.
Does swallowing in 108/15 count as completed ingestion with horns still protruding, or an attempted act with a persistent obstructing result? The ko-Preterit form is retained.
Check PrS 24/23 against inherited prs 56/36 citation numbering before changing the reference.

Jan 4.I/512: segment bləʕʕe, identify agent and object, and establish whether the speaker accepted, tolerated or could not stomach the statement. No new figurative meaning is published before this is resolved.
Human, fish, grain and animal patients retain literal swallowing. Fantasy predators do not create a separate sense. meqəm gives contextual anteriority to simple Preterit bləʕole.
Das Jonas-/Qiṭos-Ereignis bestätigt wörtliches Verschlingen mit weiblichem Agens und implizitem menschlichem Patienten; R1 enthält bereits fünf Preterit-Beispiele.
